Rashi on Eruvin 51b:1:1.hebrew: עני הוא דאקילו רבנן גביה - הבא בדרך ואין עמו פת — הוא דאקילו רבנן גביה: לומר "שביתתי במקומי" כשאינו מכיר אילן או גדר, או למכיר — לומר "שביתתי במקום פלוני":
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:1:1.english: It is [only] a pauper that the Sages were lenient with him - One who is traveling on the road and does not have bread with him — it is regarding him that the Sages were lenient: to say, “My [Shabbat] residence is in my place” when he does not recognize a tree or a fence; or, for one who recognizes [a landmark], to say, “My [Shabbat] residence is in such-and-such a place.”

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:1:2.hebrew: אבל עשיר - כגון יושב בביתו, לא זו ולא זו:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:1:2.english: However, a wealthy person - such as [one] sitting in his house, [is permitted] neither this nor that.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:2:1.hebrew: עיקר עירוב ברגל - ״שביתתי תחתי״, אפילו לעשיר, אם יצא והחשיך — זהו עיקר מצות עירוב. כדתני: ״לא אמרו לערב בפת כו'״, אלמא עיקר תקנת עירוב לר' יהודה ברגל היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:2:1.english: The primary [ordinance of] eiruv is by foot - [Declaring] "My resting place is beneath me" — even for a wealthy person, if he went out and darkness fell — this is the primary mitzvah of eiruv. As it is taught: "They only said to establish an eiruv with bread, etc." Evidently, according to Rabbi Yehuda, the primary enactment of eiruv is by foot.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:1.hebrew: זהו שאמרו חכמים - דמשמע דעיקר תקנתא לאו הכי הואי, אלא קולא בעלמא הוא שאמרו אצל העני לערב ברגליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:1.english: This is what the Sages said - For [this phrasing] implies that the primary enactment was not this [way], but rather it is merely a leniency that they stated regarding a poor person, [allowing him] to establish an eiruv with his feet.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:2.hebrew: מאן קאמר ליה ר"מ - דאמר עיקר עירוב בפת:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:2.english: Who says it? Rabbi Meir - For he says [that] the primary [enactment of an] eiruv is with bread.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:3.hebrew: ואהיכא קאי אאינו מכיר או שאינו בקי בהלכה - ואמר ״שביתתי תחתי״, עלה קאמר ר"מ: ״וזהו שאמרו״. כלומר, דאפילו להאי דאמר ״במקומי״, קולא הוא דאקילו רבנן גביה, אבל לא זהו עיקר תקנת עירוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:3.english: And to what is it referring? To: "He does not recognize, or is not well-versed in the halakha" - and said: "My Shabbat residence is beneath me" — regarding that [clause], Rabbi Meir said: "And this is what they said." That is to say, even for this one who says "[My Shabbat residence is] in my place," it is a leniency that the Rabbis granted him, but this is not the primary ordinance of an eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:4.hebrew: ולא אמרו לערב בפת - דמשמע דעיקר עירוב, כי איתקן — ברגל איתקן, ולא אמרו בפת אלא להקל על העשיר:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:4.english: And they did not say to establish an eiruv with bread - For [this] implies that the primary [enactment of] eiruv, when it was instituted, was instituted [to be established] on foot, and they said [to establish an eiruv] with bread only to be lenient for the wealthy person.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:4:1.hebrew: מחלוקת במקום פלוני - דאין כאן לא עירוב בפת ולא עירוב ברגל, אלא אמירה בעלמא — עלה קאמר ר"מ: עני — אין, עשיר — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:4:1.english: The dispute is [regarding] "in such-and-such place" - For here there is neither an eiruv with bread nor an eiruv by foot, but mere speech — regarding this, Rabbi Meir said: A pauper, yes; a wealthy person, no.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:4:2.english: However, “In my location,” everyone agrees, both a pauper and a wealthy person - For the primary [form of] eiruv is by foot:

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:5:1.hebrew: זהו שאמרו חכמים - דמשמע דעיקר תקנתא לאו הכי הואי, אלא קולא בעלמא הוא שאמרו אצל העני לערב ברגליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:5:1.english: This is what the Sages said - Which implies that the primary enactment was not like this, but rather it is merely a leniency that they stated regarding a pauper, to establish an eiruv by foot.

Tosafot on Eruvin 51b:3:1.hebrew: ואהיכא קאי אאינו מכיר - ולא בעי למימר דקאי א"מי שבא בדרך וחשכה לו", ודברי הכל — דמוכחא מתני' דבמאי דפליגי ר"מ ורבי יהודה איירי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 51b:3:1.english: "And to which [clause] is it referring? To 'If he is not familiar'" - And [the Gemara] did not want to say that it refers to [the case of] "one who was coming along the way and it grew dark for him," and [that it is] the opinion of all, because the Mishnah proves that it is dealing with that which Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda dispute.
